# infisical_pam_account_kubernetes (Resource)

Create and manage Kubernetes accounts in Infisical PAM. The connection is tested when the account is created or its connection changes. Only Machine Identity authentication is supported for this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    infisical = {
      # version = <latest version>
      source = "infisical/infisical"
    }
  }
}

provider "infisical" {
  host = "https://app.infisical.com" # Only required if using self hosted instance of Infisical, default is https://app.infisical.com
  auth = {
    universal = {
      client_id     = "<machine-identity-client-id>"
      client_secret = "<machine-identity-client-secret>"
    }
  }
}

resource "infisical_pam_account_kubernetes" "prod" {
  name        = "prod-cluster-admin"
  folder_id   = "<folder-id>"
  template_id = "<kubernetes-template-id>"

  connection_details = {
    url             = "https://k8s.prod.internal:6443"
    ssl_certificate = file("prod-ca.pem")
  }

  credentials = {
    auth_method          = "gateway-kubernetes-auth"
    namespace            = "infisical"
    service_account_name = "pam-admin"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `connection_details` (Attributes) How to reach the Kubernetes target. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--connection_details))
- `credentials` (Attributes) The credentials of the account. Secrets are never read back, so changes made outside of Terraform, such as rotation, aren't detected. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credentials))
- `folder_id` (String) The ID of the folder the account is in. Changing it moves the account.
- `name` (String) The name of the account, unique in its folder. Must be lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, at most 64 characters.
- `template_id` (String) The ID of the account template the account uses, which must be a `kubernetes` template.

### Optional

- `description` (String) An optional description of the account.
- `gateway_id` (String) The ID of the gateway to connect through instead of the template's.
- `gateway_pool_id` (String) The ID of the gateway pool to connect through instead of the template's.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the account.

<a id="nestedatt--connection_details"></a>
### Nested Schema for `connection_details`

Required:

- `url` (String) The URL of the Kubernetes API server.

Optional:

- `ssl_certificate` (String) The PEM-encoded CA certificate to verify the API server with.
- `ssl_reject_unauthorized` (Boolean) Whether to reject an API server certificate that isn't trusted. Defaults to true.


<a id="nestedatt--credentials"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credentials`

Required:

- `auth_method` (String) How the account authenticates: `service-account-token` with a stored token, or `gateway-kubernetes-auth` through the gateway as `service_account_name` in `namespace`.

Optional:

- `namespace` (String) The namespace of the service account, for the `gateway-kubernetes-auth` auth method.
- `service_account_name` (String) The name of the service account, for the `gateway-kubernetes-auth` auth method.
- `service_account_token` (String, Sensitive) The service account token, for the `service-account-token` auth method.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# This will import the Kubernetes PAM account by its ID.
# Secrets are never read back, so set the credentials in the configuration after importing.
terraform import infisical_pam_account_kubernetes.example <account_id>
```
